findings.entity: Dancer's raised right arm and its mirror image
findings.description: During the first arm raise, especially at 00:01.250–00:01.750, the real arm is already steeply raised toward vertical, with the wrist well above the head, while the reflected arm remains extended outward on a substantially lower diagonal. The reflection reaches the overhead position later. The simultaneous difference in elevation relative to the head is visible in resolved frames, rather than being a blurred-hand artifact.

findings.entity: Dancer's right hand relative to her pelvis
findings.description: At 00:05.250 and 00:05.500, the real right hand passes behind the pelvis and visibly overlaps the buttock from the rear view. At those same instants, the reflected hand lies visibly across the front of the pelvis. A mirror cannot relocate a hand from behind the body to in front of it; viewing angle does not explain the contradictory body occlusion.

findings.entity: Dancer's overhead right elbow and forearm
findings.description: From approximately 00:07.000 through 00:09.750, the real dancer holds her right arm nearly straight overhead while the reflection holds a distinctly bent elbow with the forearm angled inward over the head. At the sharp 00:08.000 frame, the real upper arm and forearm are nearly aligned but the reflected arm forms a pronounced corner. This persists during the held pose, so motion blur or a transient timing ambiguity cannot explain it.
